Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
32-year-old male with 1.5–2-month history of recurrent transient right-sided sensory and motor episodes; referred urgently to TIA clinic.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Recurrent episodes of right-hand pins-and-needles with transient weakness of right arm and leg, noted gait change.  
• Onset/progression: Began ~6–8 weeks ago, initially weekly to monthly; now occurring a couple of times daily. Each episode lasts a few days, then resolves.  
• Associated symptoms during episodes: Difficulty holding coffee cup, sensation of something in throat; denies speech or visual disturbance. Reports fatigue, generalized weakness, intermittent nausea between episodes.  
• Pertinent negatives: No current symptoms at time of consult. No swallowing difficulty outside episodes; speech and vision unaffected.  
• Past medical history: None reported.  
• Family history: Father with carotid surgery for stroke prevention.  
• Medications: Aspirin 75 mg once daily (self-initiated; dose/route/frequency documented).  
• Allergies: Penicillin.  
• Social: Non-smoker; lives with wife; employed as plastic-surgery doctor. Preventive care: Prior cholesterol, blood pressure, and diabetes screening reported normal.

Examination:
• No vitals or physical examination findings documented. Patient asymptomatic during consult.

Impression:
Recurrent transient neurological deficits concerning for transient ischaemic attacks (TIA).

Plan:
• Urgent referral to TIA / stroke clinic; expected appointment within 1–2 days (before weekend).  
• Anticipated investigations: Carotid Doppler ultrasound, brain imaging, additional stroke risk evaluation.  
• Safety-netting: Attend A&E immediately if symptoms recur and are prolonged or persistent; contact GP if any delay in clinic appointment or further episodes.  
• Provided TIA clinic and PALS contact numbers in consultation notes for patient to expedite scheduling.  
• GP to submit referral immediately.

Quality checks:

● Missing typical elements: No vitals, neurological examination, full medication list, alcohol intake.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional connectivity issues but clinical content understandable.
